subject: problems with predict() on generated variables from poly(), splines::bs(), etc.

messages.author: 28ebcbb80d991124
messages.subject: problems with predict() on generated variables from poly(), splines::bs(), etc.
parts:
Hello-

I was recently working with a student who ran into problems when making predictions from pcount() using orthogonal polynomials via poly() compared to raw polynomials (fit either with I() or poly(..., raw = TRUE) ).  I poked around a bit and found that the predict methods don't appear to be working correctly for "generated" variables like those from poly(), splines::bs(), scale(), etc.  I didn't see any previous discussion about this so thought I would bring it up here.

Here's a little example to show very different predictions from a quadratic relationship fit with poly() vs I(variable^2):

library(unmarked)

data(mallard)
mallardUMF <- unmarkedFramePCount(mallard.y, siteCovs = mallard.site,
                                  obsCovs = mallard.obs)
fm.mallard1 <- pcount(~ 1 ~ elev + I(elev^2) + offset(length), mallardUMF, K = 30)
fm.mallard2 <- pcount(~ 1 ~ poly(elev, degree = 2) + offset(length), mallardUMF, K = 30)

# Take first 5 values of original data for prediction
dat = data.frame(length = mallard.site$length[1:5],
                 elev = mallard.site$elev[1:5],
                 othervar = 1:5)

# Predictions from 2 models should be same/very similar
predict(fm.mallard1, type = "state", newdata = dat)
#>    Predicted         SE      lower     upper
#> 1 1.01396362 0.14753356 0.76237912 1.3485708
#> 2 0.48184096 0.06512837 0.36970087 0.6279961
#> 3 0.08689944 0.02133615 0.05370616 0.1406080
#> 4 0.17282331 0.04419640 0.10469431 0.2852867
#> 5 0.12698742 0.01577647 0.09954293 0.1619985

predict(fm.mallard2, type = "state", newdata = dat)
#>      Predicted           SE        lower        upper
#> 1 4.994202e+02 6.322692e+02 4.176759e+01 5.971628e+03
#> 2 8.780117e+01 1.235498e+02 5.568366e+00 1.384436e+03
#> 3 1.115903e-05 2.186476e-05 2.397735e-07 5.193400e-04
#> 4 9.999348e-06 4.019014e-05 3.791035e-09 2.637458e-02
#> 5 3.372450e+00 1.019707e+01 8.999533e-03 1.263779e+03

It turns out this disparity is because the new data for predictions has a new transformation applied to it to make orthogonal variables instead of using the transformation based on the original data.  You can see this by comparing the a model.frame using the new dataset of the first 5 original values to the original transformation of the original data.

model.frame( paste0("~", fm.mallard2@formula[3]), data = dat) # new data, new transformation
#>   poly(elev, degree = 2).1 poly(elev, degree = 2).2 offset(length)
#> 1              -0.42107325               0.50870575          0.801
#> 2              -0.37760519               0.08895565          0.115
#> 3               0.50026073              -0.37353885         -0.479
#> 4               0.58814181               0.42116410          0.315
#> 5              -0.28972410              -0.64528666         -1.102

poly(mallard.site$elev, degree = 2)[1:5, ] # original data, original transformation
#>                 1           2
#> [1,] -0.076030699  0.06829479
#> [2,] -0.073048986  0.05876529
#> [3,] -0.012831347 -0.06541581
#> [4,] -0.006803101 -0.07068313
#> [5,] -0.067020740  0.04047351

Predict functions like predict.lm appear to automagically deal with orthogonal polynomials fit with poly() by keeping information on the original transformation.  This is done with the helper function makepredictcall() and the predvars argument in the terms.object function to keep the information for model.frame() to use.

There may be sophisticated ways to deal with this.  One (simplish?) approach would be to change how the model matrix is calculated in the predict functions for data.frames to carry the original transformation along with terms().  This complicates the offset calculation, though.  Something like:

formula <- fm.mallard2@formula
stateformula <- as.formula(paste0("~", formula[3]))

# Possible fix to add predvars from original data
     # for use in model matrix with terms()
terms <- terms( model.frame(stateformula, data = fm.mallard2@data@siteCovs) )

# Now the newdata data transformation matches original
( Xmat <- model.matrix(terms, data = dat) ) # new data, original transformation
#>   (Intercept) poly(elev, degree = 2)1 poly(elev, degree = 2)2
#> 1           1            -0.076030699              0.06829479
#> 2           1            -0.073048986              0.05876529
#> 3           1            -0.012831347             -0.06541581
#> 4           1            -0.006803101             -0.07068313
#> 5           1            -0.067020740              0.04047351
#> attr(,"assign")
#> [1] 0 1 1
poly(mallard.site$elev, degree = 2)[1:5, ] # original data, transformation
#>                 1           2
#> [1,] -0.076030699  0.06829479
#> [2,] -0.073048986  0.05876529
#> [3,] -0.012831347 -0.06541581
#> [4,] -0.006803101 -0.07068313
#> [5,] -0.067020740  0.04047351

# Getting offset takes an extra step
offset <- model.offset( model.frame(terms, data = dat) )

# Predictions now same to 3ish decimal places
exp( linearComb(fm.mallard2, Xmat, type = "state", offset = offset)@estimate )
#> [1] 1.01345736 0.48168078 0.08700687 0.17303138 0.12698479

predict(fm.mallard1, type = "state", newdata = dat)$Predicted
#> [1] 1.01396362 0.48184096 0.08689944 0.17282331 0.12698742

I found similar issues when I used splines::bs() and scale() directly in pcount(), which is what made me realize this may be bigger than poly().

Regards,
Ariel

Hi Ariel,

Thanks for bringing this up. I filed a bug report here. I think predict() needs to be updated to deal with these issues and several others identified earlier. Any interest in contributing a patch? 

Richard
